title: 永恒与星辰与日常
description:
“In this world, there are things we’re told we can’t do but are allowed to do anyway, and things we can do but shouldn’t.”

When an elegant Bloodkin and a clumsy witch suddenly enter your quiet life, how will an ordinary person like you learn to live with them?

Your brief but precious time under one roof is filled with laughter and surprises. Whether you’re out shopping, playing games together, or sharing what’s on your mind late at night, each little moment brings you closer.

Little by little, you come to understand one another. Three lives that once seemed worlds apart begin to intertwine through this chance encounter. You discover the warmth of having a place to call home, even as the gap between your lifespans and the pressures of everyday life put your bonds to the test.

Every choice you make shapes the story, leading to one of four very different endings.

Will you risk taking on an eternal life and become their companion? Or will you cherish the present and keep the promise you made to each other in the fleeting time you have together?

The choice is yours.

Voiced by w小璃 (Chinese) / 猫乃緒みみ (Japanese)
Age 300+
Birthday October 31
Height 147 cm
Race Bloodkin
Personality Proud, hates hassle, aloof on the outside but warm-hearted underneath

“Hmph. It’s not like I stayed in the human world just for you!”

A young Bloodkin lady who unexpectedly barges into Lin Xiaocou’s home. Elegant and haughty at first glance, she’s really a homebody who hates anything troublesome.

Proud and sharp-tongued, Elysia has a knack for pointing out exactly what makes Lin Xiaocou’s situation so awkward. She teases him from time to time and makes all sorts of requests that are “not exactly difficult, just a lot of trouble.” Beneath her icy exterior, she’s warm-hearted and struggles to say how she really feels. Whenever she’s unsure of herself, she hides it behind an air of arrogance. She enjoys spending time with Lin Xiaocou and feels most at ease around him.

After three hundred years, Elysia had grown tired of the same old routine in her ancient castle. She ran away from home and stumbled upon Lin Xiaocou’s place, which she decided would make a “rather decent temporary base.” She likes to play the detached observer, but as the days pass, she grows curious about the fleeting lives humans lead and finds herself growing attached to them.

Voiced by 舟玄 (Chinese) / 雪乃しろ (Japanese)
Age 100+
Birthday March 14
Height 145 cm
Race Witch
Personality Cheerful, clumsy, endlessly curious, and sensitive

“…I’m not an idiot. I just didn’t want to face a reality that was far too cruel.”

A witch who unexpectedly ends up in Lin Xiaocou’s home. A magical accident stopped her from growing.

Bright and cheerful, Stella is also clumsy and prone to causing trouble. Beneath her carefree demeanor lies a sensitive heart and a quiet sadness that’s easy to miss. She tends to solve problems with dazzling magic and hide her worries behind a smile.

She’s endlessly curious about the world and firmly believes that having fun is what matters most in life. When her emotions get the better of her, she can become surprisingly vulnerable, though sometimes she lets those feelings show in full force. She feels safe around Lin Xiaocou and gradually learns to show him who she really is.

Stella spent years training under a great witch. Once she could hold her own, she set off on her own travels. A teleportation accident sent her straight into Lin Xiaocou’s home. One taste of the desserts in his fridge was enough to make her decide to stay. She may cause the occasional mishap, but she’s always trying her best to fit into human life.

• Playtime 3–5 hours

• Script length Approximately 72,000 words

• CGs 16, excluding variations

• SD CGs 6, excluding variations

description_short: Our Brief Eternity is a visual novel in which you play as Lin Xiaocou, an ordinary office worker whose quiet life is turned upside down when two girls from another world unexpectedly move in. Amid the warmth, comedy, and chaos of everyday life together, can you find a happy ending for everyone?
